Incredible. Animal Behaviorial Specialist Brunite at your service. Humans are a rarity in these parts...
Well, normally they are, at least. The last time I saw some was actually...
Wait. You were at the Linking! You saved our prince!
Well, we helped out a bit.
Please, please, you're far too modest. I doubt any of us would have gotten out of there alive were it not for your efforts.
And... me doubly so, it'd seem. Thank you for saving me once again.
We didn't have to do much, we're able to get a better vantage up here anyway.
Oh? And what are you scouting out, if I may ask?
We're headed out to the Misty Thicket. It'll be quite the journey.
What'd you learn about the behaviors of the Rockwolves? That they're hungry?
Well, actually, yes.
They seem to designate members of their pack to hunt, while others serve other purposes.
For example, the one at your feet there, its stone hide is closely related to sandstone. Hunters will sharpen their teeth by gnawing on its hide, like you'd sharpen your blade on a whetstone.
Sounds... useful, actually.
They metabolize both meat and stone, with different Rockwolves prioritizing different stone and mineral types to change their hides in accordance with what the pack needs.
I'd imagine you were acting in self-defense when you fought against the pack earlier. Well, it seems they're missing a handful of crucial roles now.
Maybe there's something that can be done for your journey...

Brunite details his plans. He'd originally wanted to use the wolves as mounts to help his people return back to their home once things were sorted with the Soulsmiths, but maybe with your help, he could expidite his plans, in exchange for letting you bring some of the wolves with you. They already seem plenty docile with you around, what's the harm in trying, right? 

You return to the capitol, and run the idea of starting a breeding program for the Rockwolves to the king, who simply laughs and waves his hand, seemingly letting the Archivist write down and deal with aquiring the materials to set up a place to store, raise, and train wolves, assuming they don't break out and eat you.

Steps.Description: 我浑身都湿透了，真难受。
Steps.CompletedDescription: I just want to find the beast and get back home.

Dialogue.DialogueText: The wolves are equal parts stone and organic, and with sufficent meat and sources of minerals, they grow much faster than you'd ever expect. In conjunction with preparing a route to the Misty Thicket, you frequently stop in to help Brunite with the Rockwolf study, creating wolves that didn't seem to appear naturally before. Soon enough, by the time you're ready to head out, you have three wolves with hides made of a material similar to quartz, hoping it'd be light enough for travel but hard enough to protect the beasts from any kind of dangerous monsters you may come across in the countryside.
I can't believe it! Rockwolves feel like they were made to be domesticated. Most of them are generally of good temperment, and they're so friendly too!
Milkbone here hardly stops licking me! I'm shocked at how fast they can grow under controlled conditions, too, it reminds me of growing crystals as a boy.
Are you sure that Milkbone isn't just seeing if you'd be a good addition to her hide? Flamberians are mostly stone, right?
I... hadn't considered that.
[Companion Name] be nice, I'm sure she's just a friendly, mostly feral wolf.
Are you sure you want to join us though, Brunite? The Misty Thicket is a long ways away.
We're just scouting a path and locating that monster that attacked the Linking, but we'll almost definitely get into some trouble at some point.
And miss the opportunity to see how the first wolves we've bred behave in uncontrolled conditions? Not a chance!

Atop the quartz rockwolves, you make extrodinary time. The beasts are fast, incredibly easy to care for, and defend themselves well enough that you feel comfortable sleeping through the night without anyone on watch. Despite his shaky introduction, Brunite proves to be quite capable while travelling to the Misty Wetlands with you, though he does still jump a bit whenever Milkbone licks him, wondering if [Companion Name]'s joke held any truth.

Finding the Shambling Beast will be like finding a needle in a haystack - and that's if it's even here in the first place - but you trudge into the wetlands regardless. The Misty Wetlands have both mist and wetland in abundance, and you frequently have to stop and cut your way through underbrush or use lumber to cross particularly deep stretches of water, especially with your heavy Rockwolves accompanying you.

Steps.Description: 可是他们先动的手。
Steps.CompletedDescription: I wonder what they may have...

Dialogue.DialogueText: As you sink your axe into yet another tree to cross another endless stretch of water, a flaming bolt glances your shoulder and sinks into the thick bark. You drop your axe and whip your head around to see the burning shilloette of a Flamberian far behind you, with a hefty crossbow held aloft. You cry out and everyone dives into the water, narrowly avoiding further projectiles. A volley of similar bolts follows soon after, peppering the ground and trees around you, your party, and mounts. You poke your head out of the water and see [Companion Name] fire a bolt of magic that freezes the water in the air, providing a thin shield against the attacks' bolts.
Those look like Flamberians!
I fear you're right. I hope the two of you are... capable of dealing with them?
If we have to. Any clue on why they're out here, and what problem they'd have with us?
I mean, you're one of them, no?
Not all Flamberians were too interested in peace with the Naladasi.
I'm sure the defectors have some way of identifying one another, and I'm sure I don't look the part.
Any idea on if this will cause any problems for us later on down the line?
Oh, I highly doubt it! There's a reason why they're hiding all the way out here.
Those that are willing to reject the Naladasi with violence aren't welcome in our kingdom.
Plus, they fired first.

That's enough for the two of you. Brunite gets your mounts to cover while you and [Companion Name] do your best to move towards the Flamberians as quietly as you can through the wetland bogs. Shrouded by the mist and setting sun, you're upon them before they even know it. You reach up from the water and drag one of the attackers under, silencing them as quickly as you can. The Flamberian next to him cries out, and the group is thrown into chaos.

Steps.Description: 准是我们要找的东西。
Steps.CompletedDescription: Here we are.

Dialogue.DialogueText: You and [Companion Name] pant in the mist, happy to be done with such messy work. Killing monsters is one thing, but it's always a little bit different to be fighting against human - or human adjacent - opponents, even if they're the aggressors. Brunite brings your rockwolves over once the sounds of fighting die down, trying to avert his eyes from the dead dwarves in the water.
You two are... efficient.
I'm sorry. They didn't seem to be too interested in talking through things.
We didn't have much choice in the matter.
Oh, don't get me wrong, I won't shed any tears for them.
They probably feared we'd give them up to Flamberian authorities if we found them out here, and thought it'd be better to silence us.
The two of you are just...
I can't think of many people who could move that quickly and leave that much death in their wake. Regardless of the reason.

Brunite grimaces as Milkbone starts to sniff the corpse of one of the attackers, and pulls her away from the body. You and [Companion Name] start to go through the defectors' posessions and find a map and various plans they'd made. Several drafts of ransom notes which lead you to believe they intended to kidnap Prince Cintak at some point... they were ambitious if nothing else. They seemed to have a nearby camp, but what interests you far more is an old ruined castle, the Flamberians had marked, circled, and drawn several warnings of "Death" and "Stay away" around. Seems like a good place to start your search. As you get closer to the old ruined castle, you find tracks that stick out in the murk. Tracks made by hundreds of pairs of arms.

CompletionDialogue.DialogueText:
The Shambling Beast made a mess of a trail through the Misty Thicket, and you wager you'd be able to follow it all the way out pretty easily, now that you've found its trail. Downed trees, a huge gouge through the ground thats already filled with water, and occasional lumps of flesh are pretty telling that you're on the right track. As you get closer and closer to what you presume would be the castle, the stench of death seems to hang in the air, which is impressive for such a horrid bog that already doesn't smell like a bundle of roses.

The two of you leave Brunite and the Rockwolves behind, trusting in your ability to move more quietly and take up less space than huge beasts with stone for fur. You follow the trail until you find what the Flamberians detailed on their map. Row upon row of corpses are pinned to the outer walls of a ancient castle. All of the bodies are seemingly frozen in space, but doubtlessly alive, since the wall adornments seem to moan and twitch from time to time. The mist-shrouded moat surrounding the castle does little to brighten the image in your mind. You let out an involentary shiver as you gaze up at the macbre sight.

[Companion Name] pulls you away, sure that the monster you're looking for is within the walls. This is definitely not something you can take on alone. It's time to see just how serious King Oyadazminis is about going to war, because it'll take quite the siege to bring down these walls. The journey back is much faster than your journey in, perhaps in part due to the back you know you'll have dry feet for the first time in a while. It's still quite the trek to return to the capitol, but it's comparatively smooth sailing than your trip to the Misty Thicket.

Quest.Description: 攻破迷雾要塞——斩杀跛行兽的武器已经备好，通往那座被炼魂师占据的古堡的路也已打通。辛塔克王子和雷迪洛克公主将率领族人出征，由你和[Companion Name]打头阵。

Steps.Description: 真想早点看看它们上阵是什么样。
Steps.CompletedDescription: We should get some rest.

Dialogue.DialogueText:
The path to the Misty Keep is plotted, a weapon to slay the Shambling Beast is strapped to your back, and things are slowly returning to normal in Koganusan. As you walk through the outer courtyard of the palace, you notice a large number of guards out and training against one another, with the occasional Flamberian even dotting their ranks - holdovers from the Linking that haven't been able to start the trek back to their homeland yet, and have decided to accompany the prince until he sees it fit to return.

When you enter the throne room, King Oyadazminis looks down from his seat with a knowing expression.
You're ready, aren't you?
I believe we are.
It's been many long years since we actively sought dealings with your kind, but what transpired at the Linking has given me much to think about.
Though I doubt most humans would be willing to help even a fraction as much as the two of you have, perhaps we've been... avoidant, for far too long.
Once those who attacked my people are burried in thier marsh, we'll send an envoy or two around. Let your people know that we'd be willing to entertain more than a few tourists, from time to time.
The world would be much better off for it.
You know they would be. We'll see if your fancy nobles can stay standing after a single glass of fine Naladasi liqour.
But, as much as I'd like to, I can't entertain the thought of festivities yet.
We've read over your reports and path to the Soulsmiths' keep.
As the king has so kindly promised, our people are at your disposal, though we'll be joining you as well.
As will my daughter... Try as I might, she refuses to stay off the battlefield, despite her injuries. The...
...Prince, seems to have taken a liking to my daughter, and is joining her.
We'd be fortunate to have the four of you alongside us, but wouldn't that be... dangerous for you all?
What kind of father would I be if I let my daughter fight my battles for me?
The king has also expressed interest in making sure nothing... untoward occ-
Ahem. We've prepared several wagons. I hear that your little breeding program with the Rockwolves has gone well?
We feel they'd be far better for handling any outdoor excursions than our current beasts of burden. Brunite was more than happy to help create some wolves that could help.
It sounds like we're just about ready then, yes?
We'll head out to prepare.

As you leave the palace, the most of training guards have already mobilized, with the remainer saluting the two of you as you pass by. You meet Brunite at the caverns set aside for the Rockwolf breeding program, and even he dawns an axe and simple armor. He brings the two of you your wolves, then takes a seat upon Milkbone and takes off down a long line of pens, cutting open the fences as he runs along, a growing pack of Stonewolves following behind him as he charges through the caverns and out of the caverns.

It's a little startling to see just how many wolves can be made in the right conditions, and hope that Brunite hasn't made too much of a fuss in the capitol. Despite the sight, many citizens cheer after you as you race through the city and out into the fresh air above. The pack slows as you step outside to see a large procession of Naladasi with armed wagons, some topped with braziers you imagine are to ward off the mists of the thicket.

There are numerous shouts as you arrive, but not because of you, it's because of the similarly sized horde growing in the distance. A large, orderly rank of Flamberians march towards the Naladasi, carrying large waving banners that make the whole army appear as if they're on fire. You spot Prince Cintak flag down king Oyadazminis, and the two of them march out to meet the army. An hour passes before the army continues its advance, banners now down. Hopefully that's a good thing?

The Prince announces that due to the silence that followed after the Linking, the Flamberians had reason to suspect the Naladasi had attacked the procession and kidnapped him, but he's informed his mother - the queen - of the full situation, and the army that was sent to attack the Naladasi are instead joining them to attack Soulsmiths. Apperently.

The journey back out to the Misty Thicket starts tense, but as more and more stories are traded between the rank and file, the dwarves stoke one another's passion towards their shared enemy, and find themselves growing closer in the process.

The wagons are pulled around to create a wall of sorts a few hours out from the Misty Keep, and you and [Companion Name] keep yourselves busy by helping to prepare the massive bolts that'll be loaded into the ballista-carrying wagons.

Steps.Description: 得抢在那些黑影前头，把人拉上来。
Steps.CompletedDescription: We did what we could.

Dialogue.DialogueText:
You're pleased to take a bit of time to yourself, even if it is to do more work. The journey over had been long and tiring, constantly riding between the ranks and guiding troops. The Flamberian queen has repeatedly called for your attention, but with as many moving parts as this war procession has had, you simply haven't had the time. Thankfully, Prince Cintak has reassured you that his mother is aware of the stakes and your part in keeping everything moving, and is more than happy to wait. You lay down after having earned your rest, and try to calm your nerves before finally falling to sleep.

After nowhere near enough time, you open your eyes to the daylight, you realize... there shouldn't be daylight. You were in a covered wagon. You look around and notice that four Flamberians have lifted your cot and carried you out in front of the queen. [Companion Name] is in a similarly dazzed, groggy state as yourself, both of you seemingly having been tired and secure enough to sleep through the... basically kidnapping. Prince Cintak stands beside his mother, mortified, and shoots you an apologetic look.
It is a pleasure to finally see the faces of my son's saviors.
I apologize for disrupting your sleep, but I wished to make myself known to you before we are to head into battle alongside one another.
I- I- Good morning, your excellency, queen...
Rest, child. I've done away with my name long ago, like all those who ascend to my rank. You may refer to me as the Flame.
I tried to get her to hold off a while longer, but she was insistant.
Pleased to meet you, your grace, but... may I ask why you've brought us here?
From what I've heard, the two of you are the reason my son still breathes.
My nation is in your debt, as am I. Were it not for your efforts, my people would have surely clashed against the Naladasi, and we'd be all the worse for it.
We were just doing what is right. The Soulsmiths... they've torn apart so many homes, our own included.
I'm just glad we were able to get to him in time.
As am I.
I just wanted to bring it to your attention that I'm endlessly thankful for your assistance, and for your efforts, I wish to reward you once we return to our homeland. I'd like to-
She wants to show off that she can give you more than the Naladasi and keep you around as my personal bodyguards.
Well, we're flattered, but...
My darling little lava rock is right! You're heroes and should be treated as such! AND I find it outrageous that that cheapskate king has you sleeping in a cart!
Are you sure the two of you want to be on the front lines?

Perhaps the three of you, or four since my precious son seems to have a thing for that cute little Naladasi princess, can wait back here while we level the castle of those rotten Soulsmiths for ever daring to-
Oh Flames, mother!
Shush dear, you can't fault a mother for trying to keep her baby safe.
Since you're all so determined to join us on the battlefield, see to it that he's safe, will you?
Of course, we'll do our best to make sure as many people make it back alive as we can.
Please do... I can't lose my son a second time.

The queen seems to be at least partially assuaged by this and nods her head. The Flamberians that carried you out now pick your cots up and carry you back to the wagon, and you try to digest what just happened.

After a couple more hours, the camp begins to shuffle once more. The dwarves break down camp and begin to move out once more. You and [Companion Name] mount your Rockwolves and lead the way, guiding the group across the more percarious bits of terrain and waiting for them to create paths to get wagons across large stretches of water when required. The castle looms in the distance, almost seemingly a source of the Misty Thicket's fog itself. The walls covered in corpses only shake the resolve of the dwarves for a moment, though you hear several utterances of how sick the people inside must be.

Soulsmiths line the walls, along with summoned beasts that remind you of bats, with mouths that are far too large.

Wagons are pulled up to form an armored wall, and then, everyone bursts into motion. Several large balls of energy soar over the walls of Misty Keep, but are burned away by Flamberian mages, or sent far off course by Naladasi mages interferring with their course. Four of the wagons' walls fall away to reveal giant ballista, which are loaded with bolts created just last night. You and [Companion Name] move through the ranks and direct their fire, and the balista shots land true. When they sink into the wall, glowing runestones across their surface glow bright, then explode, ripping large sections of the ancient castle apart. You hear and see King Oyadazminis let out a battlecry as he hefts a large javilen towards the ramparts and snaps his fingers just before contact, causing the bolt to explode in a dazzling ball of light that blows twenty Soulsmiths apart. The Archivist twists his staff in the air and halts another ball of green energy above the army before sending it back over the wall towards whatever sent it in the first place, causing the entire castle to shake with the impact.

Soulsmiths fire all manner of bolt, arrow, and magic towards the dwarves, and they return fire, but the evergrowing swarm of bat-like creatures harass the them. You watch as several dwarves are picked up by the beasts and are dropped into the moat around the castle, where large, dark shadows quickly pull the soliders under the water. Bats are burned away, and more balista shots are loosed at the walls, but with the force you're now taking, one of the balls of green energy makes it through your defenses and crashes into one of the wagons, leaving it a smoldering pile of scrap. The bats grow further in number, and your find a startling number of dwarves being carried away, while the Flamberian Queen seems to be frozen in shock. You grab a length of rope with a hook on the end, meant to scale the walls, and instead use it to fish out a dwarf from the water. Many others around you follow suit, while the back ranks cover you.

Steps.Description: 今天，那野兽非死不可。
Steps.CompletedDescription: It's over.

Dialogue.DialogueText:
You do what you can, hauling as many dwarves out of the water as you have time for. Tons of hooks fly into the water once the others catch wind of your idea. You haul up more dwarves than you can count, but as you reel in another, your rope goes taught and is ripped from your hands, then goes slack. Whatever is in the water is very, very, big.

The Flame is ripped from her trance-like state. It wasn't shock, the woman was preparing. The thicket behind the dwarves cracks and screams as a wave of golden fire washes overhead like a wave crashing on the beach. The sky is blotted out by golden flame that sweeps through the air and rips through the majority of the Soulsmiths' bats and crashes against the wall, lighting the corpses ablaze. Where they were still before, the living wall now screams at your forces, with many of them tearing away bits of their body and turning it into balls of black magic which they then pelt you with.

Each one explodes in black flashes with concussive force, sending those they hit to the ground. Another wagon is destroyed as a volley of green magic comes over the wall once more. Soulsmiths atop the wall fire at the undefended dwarves, but both races return with their own bolts in turn. Princess Redilok stands atop one of the balista wagons and charges the bolt that is fired from it. It connects with the south-western tower, and explodes with startling force. The tower groans and collapses due to the damage, Soulsmiths try in vain to jump from its collapsing weight, but land in the water amongst whatever monster they have patrolling the depths.
It's time! Their forces are scattered!
Ready the rope bolts!
For those who died at the Linking!
For all the lives the Soulsmiths have claimed!

Only two of the four balista carts still stand, but it's enough. Ropes are already tied to the large bolts which are launched and burried into the top of the drawbridge. Brunite sees to the Rockwolves and orders them to charge away from the keep, pulling the ropes taught. Another pair of bolts are launched. Then another. Then another. You lose another of the carts to a group of Soulsmiths that has flown over the wall atop giant versions of the bats that swarmed you before the golden flames burned the from the sky, but they're eventually cut down.

Finally, the drawbridge gives and comes crashing down. The path into the Misty Keep is open.  Wolves are unteathered and then sent back towards the keep, their stony bodies deflecting some of the smaller projectiles as they crash into the ranks of Soulsmiths on the other side of the gate. Flamberian and Naladasi charge side-by-side across the bridge, some stopping to pull up comrades from the water. As dwarf and Soulsmith fall, an all too familiar sight that brings back memories of the Linking washes over you. A pulse of green light, then the dead begin to move once more. The Shambling Beast is here.

You charge amongst the dwarves with [Companion Name] at your side, and you find yourself face-to-face with a Soulsmith. A butcher. A monster. She raises her staff towards you, but is carved down by Prince Cintak, who leads the charge. The man yells to those around him to clear a path.

The Shambling Beast crawls towards you, endless rows of arms churning the earth beneath it. You lift your Soulmetal-lined Blade and charge through the crowd.

CompletionDialogue.DialogueText:
With each stroke of your blade, its Soulsteel edge seems to quiver with delight. You find the blade actively pulling towards its source and relishing in the pain it inflicts upon the Shambling Beast. You carve through the beast, the blade pulls you further, and you climb atop the spongey flesh of the creature. 

Hundreds of arms grasp at you as it tries in vain to pull you off, but [Companion Name] batters them away, ripping a spike of Soulsteel from the monster and weilding it like a mallet, repeatedly crashing down upon the beast. Your sword continues to delight in cleaving through flesh, but you wrest control of it long enough to drive the sword into cage fused with the back of the Shambling Beast.

With that, another pulse of green light is unleashed and you're thrown from the creature, leaving your sword wedged in the metal of the cage. As you sail through the air, you see the undead begin to drop, but the Soulsmiths fight on. However, without support from the undead, they're far outnumbered by the dwarves. 

The Shambling Beast is dead. You've won.

You feel nothing but relief as you crash into the ground, and everything goes dark.

AstrologyObservationEvent.Observation: You study the stars carefully, but they remain silent.
The constellation offers no insight this time.
Whatever message the stars held has slipped away.
You sense a faint presence among the stars, but it quickly fades.
The constellation's light flickers without revealing its secrets.
You wait patiently for a sign, but none arrives.
You almost discern a message before it vanishes from your thoughts.
The constellation politely declines to elaborate.
You feel certain the stars judged your attempt. They offer no further comment.
Even the stars have off days.
You continue to observe the stars, confirming that they are indeed stars.
The stars insist that talking to plants helps. They refuse to comment on whether the plants listen.
The constellation warns that the tallest tree always wins an argument with a blunt axe.
The stars reveal that weeds are simply crops with exceptional confidence.
The stars suggest that planting today is wiser than promising you'll plant tomorrow.
The constellation claims every mighty Oak Tree was once a seed that ignored terrible advice.
The stars quietly remind you that chopping the tree before collecting the fruit is rarely the optimal strategy.
The stars wonder why you're not mining Coal right now.
The stars insist that hitting the rock harder is a valid mining strategy.
